name: A Stroll Around the Matrix
description: William has two arrays of numbers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ and $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_m$$$. The arrays satisfy the conditions of being convex. Formally an array $$$c$$$ of length $$$k$$$ is considered convex if $$$c_i - c_{i - 1} \lt c_{i + 1} - c_i$$$ for all $$$i$$$ from $$$2$$$ to $$$k - 1$$$ and $$$c_1 \lt c_2$$$. Throughout William's life he observed $$$q$$$ changes of two types happening to the arrays: Add the arithmetic progression $$$d, d \cdot 2, d \cdot 3, \dots, d \cdot k$$$ to the suffix of the array $$$a$$$ of length $$$k$$$. The array after the change looks like this: $$$[a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{n - k}, a_{n - k + 1} + d, a_{n - k + 2} + d \cdot 2, \dots, a_n + d \cdot k]$$$. The same operation, but for array $$$b$$$. After each change a matrix $$$d$$$ is created from arrays $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, of size $$$n \times m$$$, where $$$d_{i, j}=a_i + b_j$$$. William wants to get from cell ($$$1, 1$$$) to cell ($$$n, m$$$) of this matrix. From cell ($$$x, y$$$) he can only move to cells ($$$x + 1, y$$$) and ($$$x, y + 1$$$). The length of a path is calculated as the sum of numbers in cells visited by William, including the first and the last cells. After each change William wants you to help find out the minimal length of the path he could take.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 100, 2 \le m \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le q \le 10^5$$$), the sizes of the arrays and the number of changes. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^{12}$$$), the contents of array $$$a$$$. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_m$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le 10^{12}$$$), the contents of array $$$b$$$. Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains three integers $$$type$$$, $$$k$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$1 \le type \le 2$$$, if $$$type = 1$$$, then $$$1 \le k \le n$$$ otherwise $$$1 \le k \le m$$$, $$$1 \le d \le 10^3$$$).
output_specification: After each change, output one integer, the minimum length of the path in the constructed matrix.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1609G — A Stroll Around the Matrix [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
